title: The Lord Did What He Promised

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now the Lord was gracious to Sarah as he had said, and the Lord did for Sarah what he had promised. Sarah became pregnant and bore a son to Abraham in his old age, at the very time God had promised him. - Gen 21:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After twenty-five years of waiting, the promise finally arrives. And notice how Scripture piles up the language of faithfulness: "as he had said," "what he had promised," "at the very time God had promised." The Bible seems almost to insist on it - God did exactly what He said, exactly when He said. Nothing was left to chance or luck. This was promise kept.

Think of the long road behind this moment. Sarah had laughed in disbelief. Abraham had schemed with Hagar. Both had grown old, well past any natural hope. The years had stretched on and on, and surely there were seasons when the promise felt dead. And yet - "the Lord did for Sarah what he had promised."

There is enormous encouragement here for anyone waiting on God. His promises are not empty words that fade with time. They are anchored in His faithful character. However long the delay, however impossible the situation, "God is not human, that he should lie" (Num 23:19). What He has promised, He will do.

And notice the tender word "gracious." Isaac was not a reward Sarah earned by her patience - she hadn't been all that patient. He was a gift of grace, given at the appointed time. Every promise God has made to you in Christ rests on the same faithful, gracious God. He did it for Sarah. He will do what He has promised for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you waiting on a promise of God that feels long delayed?
- Can you trust that God will do exactly what He said, at the right time?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Faithful God, thank You that You do exactly what You promise, at exactly the right time. In my seasons of waiting, anchor me in Your faithful character. Thank You that Your promises never fail.
Amen.
